notes.title: Borderless Gaming v1.0.8
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

In my haste to release fixes, the last update (v1.0.7) was actually a duplicate of v1.0.6. Consequently, v1.0.8 includes all the fixes that were supposed to be in v1.0.7.

Additionally, v1.0.8 includes:
- [b]Super Size[/b]: This feature from the legacy Borderless Gaming is back. You can enable “Super Size” in your profile, and it will make the game borderless across all your screens.
- [b]Legacy Compatibility Issues:[/b] The last of the issues related to legacy compatibility have been resolved, and all functions should now work normally. If you’re still encountering issues that weren’t present in the legacy version, please join the Discord and let me know.
- [b]Advanced Options Checkbox[/b]: A checkbox has been added under “Advanced Options” to send a maximize command to a target game. In most cases, you won’t need this, but some games might require it. So, it’s been surfaced from the internals so you can control when it happens. It’s off by default. Games like M.U.G.E.N with the SDL_NoFrame mod I created should now properly go fullscreen.

notes.title: Borderless Gaming v1.0.6
notes.content:
Phew! What a sprint this has been. I want to express my gratitude to those who have been patient and understanding that software development is challenging. Providing support for thousands of games, spanning decades and possessing their own unique quirks, is an immense task.

However, I’m thrilled to announce that I’ve successfully conquered this task. This update resolves the last remaining bugs in the windowing engine. You no longer need to manually manage your taskbar or customize the positioning of each game with profiles; everything is set and forget.

Games like Minecraft and other titles should now function as expected like they did in legacy, and titles that weren't previously supported in legacy like Dishonored now work great.

If you encounter any other issues, please join the Discord server and ping me so I can address them promptly. You should be able to play with confidence.

- Andrew

notes.title: Borderless Gaming v1.0.5
notes.content:
[h2]Fixes[/h2]

[list]
[*]Fixed timing issues in the windowing engine - games like [b]Dishonored[/b] now work properly (use Custom Size or No Change in profile settings for best results)

[*]Various minor bug fixes and stability improvements
[/list]

[h2]New: SDL_NoFrame Proxy[/h2]

Some older SDL 1.2 based games (like M.U.G.E.N) don't support being converted to borderless windows through normal means. For these stubborn cases, I've created SDL_NoFrame - a proxy library that forces SDL 1.2 games to run borderless natively.

[b]Get it here:[/b] [url=https://github.com/andrewmd5/SDL_NoFrame]https://github.com/andrewmd5/SDL_NoFrame[/url]

Only use SDL_NoFrame if Borderless Gaming can't make the SDL 1.2 game borderless on its own. Once SDL_NoFrame has made the game borderless, you can use Borderless Gaming to make it fullscreen.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9499712/85ba222c29ff750662bc2d1a3a67064532b74230.gif[/img]

notes.title: Borderless Gaming v1.0.4
notes.content:
This completely overhauls how Borderless Gaming handles windows, fixing issues with applications that have multiple windows.

[h2]Major Changes[/h2]

[list]
[*][b]Multi-Window Support:[/b] Borderless Gaming now properly detects and manages ALL windows for each process, not just one. This fixes issues with applications that have both console and main windows, or multiple game windows

[*][b]Improved Window Matching:[/b] Profiles now correctly match and apply to specific windows rather than just the first window that has the heuristics of the 'main window' found for a process

[*][b]Better SDL Support:[/b] Added special handling for SDL windows which require different flags to properly update when made borderless
[/list]

[h2]Fixes[/h2]

[list]
[*]Fixed window detection for applications with multiple windows (console + main window)

[*]Fixed profiles not applying to the correct window when multiple windows exist

[*]Fixed window restoration issues with certain game engines

[*]Improved retry logic with exponential backoff 

[*]Fixed various edge cases with window state detection
[/list]

[h2]Technical Note[/h2]

This update properly aggregates all windows under each process and lets the matching engine select the correct one based on your profile settings. If you had issues with games showing up twice or profiles applying to the wrong window, this update should resolve those problems.

This fixes stretching issues in games like [b]The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky[/b] - Preserve Client Area and Preserve Aspect Ratio are now mutually exclusive options


[*][b]Automatic Re-application:[/b] Borderless Gaming now detects when a game resets its window state (common after cutscenes or resolution changes) and automatically re-applies your profile. This fixes issues with games like [b]Lucky Tower Ultimate[/b]
[/list]

notes.title: Borderless Gaming v1.0.0 Beta
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

You might be wondering, "v1.0.0? Aren't we on v10?" Well, yes and no. Borderless Gaming has been completely rewritten from the ground up, so it felt right to reset the version number.

[h2]Why the rewrite?[/h2]

I created Borderless Gaming almost a decade ago for a simple reason - to play Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance while chatting with friends. Since then, Windows has changed a lot, and the old codebase was struggling to keep up. Adding new features became a hassle, and maintaining backwards compatibility (even for XP!) was slowing me down.

[h2]What's new?[/h2]

[list]
[*][b]Profiles replace Favorites:[/b] I've introduced a new profile system that's more flexible and powerful.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9499712/35d805afcedf54e7fa7080b00af71e4473caac6f.gif[/img]

[*][b]DPI-aware window handling:[/b] Set custom sizes and get consistent results across different displays.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9499712/d11e960f15244f2612de9390e29f05f54ca1bfe3.gif[/img]
[/list]

[h2]Beta status and future plans[/h2]

Most features from the previous version are here, but this is a beta. I'm counting on you all to report any bugs you find. Some things, like UI localization, aren't ready yet. Don't worry - I've hired professionals to translate the app into 20+ languages for the full release.

[h2]How to join the beta:[/h2]

1. Join our Discord: [url=https://discord.com/invite/8UvpR5UgX3]https://discord.com/invite/8UvpR5UgX3[/url]
2. Check the dev updates channel under Borderless Gaming
3. Enter the password you find there into Steam:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9499712/2ba5c2f4eb11d9b10a3645c15e16af06cfefb323.png[/img]

If you have any questions, feel free to ask in the Discord. Let's make this beta great together!


PS: An important note for retro gamers out there. The versions that support XP-Windows 7 and version 10 of Borderless Gaming will still be available as branches once this new version is released.

notes.title: Borderless Gaming v10.1.0 - App Containers
notes.content:
[h2]What's New: App Containers[/h2]

App Containers let you add custom backgrounds to your games. This feature is useful for:

[list]
[*]Games that don't fill your entire screen
[*]Adding backgrounds that match your game's style
[*]Improving the look of your streams or recordings
[*]Making older games look better on modern displays
[/list]

[h3]How to Use App Containers:[/h3]

[olist]
[*]Right-click on a game in your Favorites list
[*]Hover over 'App Container' in the context menu
[*]Pick a background option (image, color, or gradient)
[*]Start your game
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9499712/a78049f874061e568666d2ae9494db70d8fe503d.jpg[/img]

[h3]Special Window Feature[/h3]

Unlike other solutions, App Containers don't change your desktop background. Instead, they create a special window that can be alt-tabbed like any other application. This means you can still multitask easily while enjoying your customized game view.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9499712/f47e463673389b1bd4d30df10599d670c253907e.gif[/img]


[h3]Examples:[/h3]

Before: Game made borderless with a custom size, no container.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9499712/c123fa84fdd2fef164f1fa24bbee984786178cc7.jpg[/img]

After: Game with custom background via App Containers
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9499712/8ad2171a46dc759c128677ace3347a45bb2db66e.png[/img]

[h2]App Containers Features:[/h2]

[list]
[*]Choose images, colors, or gradients for backgrounds
[*]Works with most games
[*]Open source code available
[/list]

[h2]Other Updates:[/h2]

[list]
[*]Fixed crash when processing certain window titles
[*]Improved CPU usage when running in the background
[*]Added support for games using Vulkan on Windows 11
[*]Updated internal libraries to latest versions
[/list]

[h2]Early Access to App Containers[/h2]

App Containers is currently available on the vnext branch on Steam. To access it:

[olist]
[*]Right-click on Borderless Gaming in your Steam library
[*]Select Properties
[*]Go to the Betas tab
[*]Choose 'vnext' from the dropdown menu
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9499712/b7bb2fb56225a14de7a569b7c1ab53eb003b0b08.png[/img]

App Containers will be available to all users in the main branch next week.

[h2]Share Your Thoughts[/h2]

We'd like to hear from you about App Containers:

[url=https://discord.com/invite/JjaFKYsbAD style=button]Discuss on Discord[/url]

[h2]For Developers[/h2]

Check out the App Containers source code:

[url=https://github.com/andrewmd5/appcontainer style=button]App Containers on GitHub[/url]

[hr][/hr]

[i]Note: Some games with anti-cheat systems might not work with App Containers. Use responsibly and check your game's terms of service.[/i]

notes.title: Update Notes for v10.0.23
notes.content:
[center][b]Update 10.0.23: Potential Startup Issue Mitigation[/b][/center]

Hello everyone,

I've just pushed version [b]10.0.23[/b] in an effort to potentially mitigate some of the startup issues a few users have been encountering. I appreciate your patience and support as I work to improve your experience with Borderless Gaming.

If you are still experiencing startup issues, I request you to check the Event Viewer on Windows to report any errors Borderless Gaming might be reporting there. Here's a quick guide on how to access the Event Viewer and find relevant error logs:

[list]
[*] Press [b]Windows Key + R[/b] to open the Run dialog.
[*] Type [b]eventvwr[/b] and press [b]Enter[/b].
[*] In the Event Viewer window, expand the [b]Windows Logs[/b] section in the left panel.
[*] Click on [b]Application[/b] to view a list of application logs.
[*] Look for any entries related to [b]Borderless Gaming[/b]. Errors are usually marked with a red error icon.
[*] Double-click on the relevant entry to view detailed information about the error.
[*] Take note of the error message and any other relevant details.
[/list]

Please report these details to me to help diagnose and resolve the issue more effectively. Your feedback is invaluable and greatly appreciated.

Thank you for your cooperation and support!

Best regards,
Andrew

[h1]Optional Dark Mode DLC Now Available![/h1]

I'm excited to announce that an optional [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2901910/Borderless_Gaming__Dark_Mode/]dark mode DLC[/url] is now available for Borderless Gaming.

With the release of v10 a few weeks ago, Borderless Gaming's internals were rewritten to improve stability, increase performance, and bring much-needed improvements to its interaction with Windows 11. I'm currently working on v11, which includes a complete UI rewrite to move away from the legacy framework I originally built nearly a decade ago. This rewrite aims to make Borderless Gaming cross-platform, sleeker, and improve the overall user experience.

To support the ongoing development and fund the work required for these significant improvements, I've released dark mode as an optional DLC. This DLC is intended to replace the previous "Donation DLC" and provides a way for the community to directly contribute to Borderless Gaming's continued development.

[h2]Why charge for dark mode?[/h2]

As the sole maintainer of Borderless Gaming, I rely on the community's support through purchases on Steam to continue dedicating time and resources to the project. I want to assure you that I would never paywall core functionality. Dark mode is a purely cosmetic addition that has not previously existed in Borderless Gaming and is not required to use the software or any of its features. By offering it as an optional DLC, it serves as a clear way for users to show their ongoing support for the project's longevity.

[h2]Regarding the achievement[/h2]

This DLC adds one new achievement. For those who are "achievement hunters" and prefer not to pay for unlocking achievements, you can still unlock it without purchasing the DLC by pressing [b]"Win" + "F7" [/b] while Borderless Gaming is focused.

[h2]Why not increase the base app price?[/h2]

Borderless Gaming offers everything you need out of the box. Raising the base price would make the Steam version and its powerful features inaccessible to many people. By offering optional DLC, those who can afford to support the project further can do so, while ensuring the base app remains affordable for everyone.

[h2]Upcoming features in v11[/h2]

v11 will bring exciting new features, including integer scaling, custom frames, a modern UI, plugins, and much more. Your support through the dark mode DLC will directly contribute to the development of these features.

I understand that some people may have strong opinions on this approach. I want to remind everyone that Borderless Gaming is freeware, and you can find the full source code, including dark mode, on [url=https://github.com/Codeusa/Borderless-Gaming]GitHub[/url] and use it without paying. By purchasing the dark mode DLC on Steam, you're funding the development of crucial new features, and if you don't want to purchase dark mode, you'll still have full access to any new features added thanks to the support and backing of the community.

As always, I'm open to your feedback and appreciate your continued support.

Click [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2901910/Borderless_Gaming__Dark_Mode/]here[/url] to purchase dark mode.

notes.title: Update Notes for Borderless Gaming v10
notes.content:
We're thrilled to announce the official release of Borderless Gaming v10 as of today! A huge shoutout to everyone who participated in testing the release candidate. Your support has been invaluable.

[b]What's New?[/b] 
In this update, you might notice minimal visual changes. That's because the focus was on enhancing performance and stability from the inside out. Key improvements include:
- Elimination of the .NET Framework dependency for a smoother experience.
- Significant reductions in crashes and stability issues for more reliable gameplay.
- Full compatibility with the latest Windows 11, ensuring everyone can enjoy their favorite games without boundaries.

[b][u]Migrating Your Settings[/u][/b]

Noticed your settings or favorites were reset? No worries! Here's a quick guide to migrate your favorites to v10 seamlessly:
1. Completely exit Borderless Gaming.
2. In your Steam library, right-click on "Borderless Gaming" and select [b]Properties -> Local Files -> Browse[/b].
3. In the installation folder, double-click "bgm.exe" to automatically transfer your favorites.

[b]Need Help?[/b]

Encountering issues or have suggestions for our next update? We're all ears!
- Report issues directly on our [url=https://github.com/Codeusa/Borderless-Gaming]GitHub page[/url].
- Share your feedback or suggestions for future releases. We're already working on some exciting visual updates for the next version, so stay tuned!

Thank you for being a part of our journey.

notes.title: Borderless Gaming 10.0 - Preview
notes.content:
[i][b]Kept you Waiting, huh?[/b][/i]

I'm excited to announce that after a significant hiatus, I'm back with a new update! The Borderless Gaming 10.0 prerelease isn't just about adding new features - it's about stepping into the future. I've ported the entire project from the .NET Framework, which it was initially built on, to the streamlined, efficient .NET 8.

The significant changes you'll find in this release include:

- [b]Updated Tech[/b]: The transition to .NET 8 ensures the software continues to run seamlessly on modern systems, giving Borderless Gaming a solid foundation for future enhancements and features.

- [b]Improved Stability[/b]: I've focused on fixing various stability issues that have occasionally impacted users in the past, ensuring a smoother, more consistent gaming experience.

- [b]Standalone Executable[/b]: No more dependencies! Borderless Gaming now operates as a standalone executable.

But this is just the beginning! I have plans for more features and improvements in the pipeline, including expanding Borderless Gaming to support macOS and Linux. This has been a long-requested feature and I'm delighted to be working towards making it a reality.

Please feel free to test out this prerelease and share your valuable feedback. Your input will be instrumental in shaping the future of Borderless Gaming. To try out the prerelease on Steam, opt-in to the beta:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9499712/b7bb2fb56225a14de7a569b7c1ab53eb003b0b08.png[/img]

And don't forget to share your feedback and request on the community hub: https://steamcommunity.com/app/388080/discussions/0/5264192561403132687/

Thank you for your continued support and happy gaming!

notes.title: Patch 9.4.7
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

In the continued effort to rewrite Borderless Gamings core code, I've pushed out a brand new update that improves performance of the application. Response times should now feel a lot smoother and CPU usage should be down.

Here is a full list of changes 

[*] New portable config file, favorites and settings saved to a single file on disk rather than registry. (All favorites/settings have been reset)
[*] Borderless Gaming can now mute/unmute games depending on their focus. Great for mult-tasking/streaming.
[*] Fixed multiple crashes.
[*] Improved resource usage. 
[*] Switched build to use highest, so users without administration privileges should still be able to launch.

Because this required a lot of changes to the core code, please report any issues you find on the forums.

notes.content:
[h1]Change log[/h1]
[list]

As always, report any issues you may be having so they can be fixed.

Thanks,

Andrew

notes.title: 8.3 is live!
notes.content:
Whats included in this update?
[list][*]Added exception handling when reading Favorites settings so that in the case of corrupt or unreadable favorites, the application may continue to load without them.  This resolve Windows 10 ThreadException[/*][*]Added more exception handling when enumerating processes to prevent issues where Windows is resuming from sleep or hibernation and a process is not responding or unavailable in an unusual way.  This resolves issue Borderless Gaming stops working after Windows resumes from sleep or hibernation[/*][*]Merged changes from SecretOnline, including adding a process to favorites by regex string and togglable application update availability check.[/*][*]Updated the program icon with a new font that’s more visible at more resolutions.[/*][*]Added an installer reference to Microsoft.Threading.Tasks.dll – code changes from steveadoo32 add non-.Net default library requirements, but had forgotten to add a reference in the installer so it was missing from deployment.  This fixes issues loading issues[/*][/list]

Enjoy!
